title: BrowserStack vs LambdaTest (Now TestMu AI): An Honest Comparison
description: BrowserStack vs LambdaTest, now TestMu AI: products, free plans and prices as of November 2026, and which suits developers, QA teams and agencies.

image.alt: BrowserStack vs LambdaTest. Card reading: same job, different prices, trial both first

blocks.v: BrowserStack vs LambdaTest is the comparison most teams make when they choose a testing cloud. Both let you test websites and apps on real devices and browsers you do not own, and both run automated tests in parallel. The differences are in pricing, free access and where each company is putting its effort.

One thing to know first: LambdaTest renamed itself TestMu AI on 12 January 2026. The company says the team, infrastructure and customer accounts stayed the same, and lambdatest.com now redirects to testmuai.com. I use both names here, because most people still search for LambdaTest.
Which is better, BrowserStack or LambdaTest?

Choose BrowserStack if you want the longest-established option, a mature visual testing product in Percy with a monthly free allowance, and free access for open source projects. Choose TestMu AI if price matters more, you want a free tier that does not expire, or you are interested in its AI test writing and its HyperExecute platform.
For a team with a real test suite, run both trials on that suite before deciding. How each one handles your own tests is worth more than any comparison, including this one.

blocks.v: Both support the common frameworks, Selenium, Playwright, Cypress and Appium among them, so moving between the two usually means changing connection settings rather than rewriting tests. Check your exact framework and version in each platform's documentation before you commit.
What do BrowserStack and LambdaTest have in common?

More than the marketing suggests. Both give you manual testing on real desktop browsers and real phones, streamed to your own browser. Both run automated tests on a cloud grid, with videos, logs and screenshots of each run. Both have a tunnel tool for testing staging and local sites, BrowserStack Local on one side and TestMu AI Tunnel, formerly LambdaTest Tunnel, on the other. Both sell visual testing, accessibility testing and test management on top.

So the decision is rarely about whether a tool can do the job at all. It is about price at your scale, how reliable and fast the sessions are for your tests, and which extra products you would actually use.
How do the free plans compare?
This is the clearest difference between them, as of November 2026:

v: BrowserStack: a free trial, which its support pages put at 30 minutes of Live, 60 minutes of Automate and 30 minutes of App Live. Percy has a free plan of 5,000 screenshots a month, and open source projects can apply for free access.

TestMu AI: free-forever tiers with no credit card. Live gives short two-minute sessions renewed monthly, Automation gives a one-time 100 minutes with 2 parallel sessions, and SmartUI gives 2,000 screenshots once.

blocks.v: Neither free offer is enough for regular testing. TestMu AI's lasts longer, while BrowserStack's lets you do more in one sitting. For a wider look at free options, including tools that have nothing to do with either company, see [[free BrowserStack alternatives|/free-browserstack-alternatives]].
BrowserStack vs LambdaTest pricing

Both list prices in US dollars per month, billed annually, with higher rates for month-to-month billing. These are the closest like-for-like plans I could match from the two official pricing pages as of November 2026:

blocks.v: Be careful with the matching, because the plans are not identical. BrowserStack's entry Live plan uses real desktop browsers, while TestMu AI's Virtual Live runs on virtual browsers. Screenshot allowances and parallel counts differ between tiers, and TestMu AI's page shows parallel options on several plans without always saying which count the headline price covers. Prices change often, so treat this table as a starting point and check both pages.
BrowserStack pricing (official page)
Each product, including Live, Automate and Percy, has its own tab with its tiers.
TestMu AI pricing (official page)
Its plans are grouped into live, automation, HyperExecute, visual and accessibility testing, with a monthly and annual toggle.
How do you run a fair trial of both?
A comparison article can only take you so far. The fairest test is to run the same small job on both platforms in the same week:

v: Pick five real tests: two manual journeys, such as a contact form and a checkout, and three automated tests you already run.
Choose the same three devices on each platform, matching what your analytics say your visitors use.
Run each automated test several times and note failures that are not caused by your code. Flaky sessions cost more time than any price difference.
Time how long a manual session takes to start and how responsive it feels from where you work.
Price the plan you would really need, with the right number of users and parallel tests, at the billing period you would really choose.

blocks.v: Write the results in one table and the decision usually makes itself. Before signing an annual contract, also ask each vendor where test data, screenshots and videos are stored and for how long, especially if you test pages that show customer details.
Where is BrowserStack stronger?

v: Track record: founded in 2011 and, by its own figures, used by more than 50,000 customers. For buyers who face procurement and security reviews, that history helps.
Percy: an established visual testing product whose free allowance renews every month.
Open source: free Live, Automate and Percy access for qualifying projects.
Real desktop browsers from the entry-level single-user Live plan.

blocks.v: Where is TestMu AI (LambdaTest) stronger?

v: Price of entry: a $15 virtual browser plan and $79 desktop automation, billed annually, undercut BrowserStack's nearest plans.
A free tier that does not expire, so you can keep an account open for occasional checks.
HyperExecute: its platform for running large test suites faster, which has its own free tier of 300 minutes.
AI focus: the new name signals where the company is heading, with KaneAI for writing tests in plain language.

blocks.v: If you want a default with no strong preference either way, start with whichever trial covers the devices your visitors actually use. Lean towards BrowserStack where clients or procurement expect an established vendor, and towards TestMu AI where budget decides. Neither is a bad choice. The bad choice is paying every month for parallel tests and users you never touch, so size the plan to the work you do today and move up when the queue of tests says you need to.

If you have not used either, start with [[how to use BrowserStack|/how-to-use-browserstack]], which walks through a first manual test on an iPhone. If you are still deciding whether a paid cloud is worth it at all, read [[BrowserStack pros and cons|/browserstack-pros-and-cons]] and [[what BrowserStack is|/what-is-browserstack]].
Frequently asked questions
Is LambdaTest the same as TestMu AI?
Yes. LambdaTest renamed itself TestMu AI on 12 January 2026. The company says the team, infrastructure and customer accounts did not change, and lambdatest.com redirects to the new site.
Is LambdaTest cheaper than BrowserStack?

At entry level, usually. As of November 2026, TestMu AI lists Virtual Live at $15 a month and desktop automation at $79, billed annually, against $29 and $99 for BrowserStack's nearest plans. Real-device manual testing is $39 a month at both.
Which has the better free plan, BrowserStack or LambdaTest?

TestMu AI's free plan lasts longer because it does not expire, but its live sessions are short. BrowserStack's trial gives more time in one go but then ends. For visual testing, BrowserStack's Percy free plan is the more generous allowance.
Can I move my tests from BrowserStack to LambdaTest?
Usually yes, without rewriting them. Both support Selenium, Playwright, Cypress and Appium, so the main change is the connection settings. Check framework versions on both sides first.
Which is better for testing on real iPhones?
Both offer real iPhones on paid plans. Test the iPhone models and iOS versions your users have on each trial, because device availability and session speed matter more than headline device counts.
